report:
On the Cranial MRI examination of your patient:
Sequences used in the examination:
Axial plane; FLAIR and T2-weighted FSE,
Sagittal plane; T2-weighted FSE,
Coronal plane; T1-weighted SE.

The fourth ventricle is of normal size and configuration. The cerebellar hemispheres, vermis, and brainstem are of normal signal intensity and morphology.

Both internal acoustic canals are of normal width. The sella is of normal morphology. Both cavernous sinuses are symmetric and of normal signal intensity.

Convexity sulci, ventricular system, and basal cisterns are prominent (cerebral atrophy).
Hyperintense chronic microangiopathic ischemic gliotic foci are noted in the periventricular and supraventricular deep white matter on T2 and FLAIR weighted examinations in the bilateral frontoparietal lobes.

The corpus callosum is of normal signal intensity and morphology.
The third ventricle is midline. No deviation is observed in the midline structures.
Extra- and intra-axial collections and mass lesions were not detected.
No findings suggestive of thrombus were detected in the dural sinuses. Mucosal thickenings causing complete loss of aeration in the left maxillary sinus and partial loss of aeration in the right maxillary sinus are observed. Aeration of other paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells is normal. Bilateral inferior turbinates are hypertrophic.

Impression:
- Multiple chronic microangiopathic ischemic gliotic foci in the periventricular and supraventricular deep white matter of the bilateral frontoparietal lobes
- Cerebral atrophy
- Mucosal thickenings causing complete loss of aeration in the left maxillary sinus and partial loss of aeration in the right maxillary sinus
